newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCC rates stay low, outlook same for Sept.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCC rates stay low, outlook same for Sept.

text.p: Middle East VLCC spot tanker rates on Friday stayed at the lower levels posted midweek amid a dearth of fresh fixtures and plentiful tonnage.
Brokers said the outlook for September didn't look much better.
Japan-bound VLCCs stayed at W65 with western voyages still only able to command about W55. No new Middle East VLCC fixtures had been reported by mid-afternoon in London.

"We estimate a total of 74 units of 21 million deadweight tonnes will be available between now and September 27 which indicates little likelihood of a real increase in rate levels of this month," said E A Gibson in a report.
But a reopening of the transatlantic arbitrage for shipments out of the British North Sea saw the first VLCC fixture for that route in more than two weeks.
Brokers said Vitol fixed a 285,000 tonne cargo on the Berge Banker travelling on September 12 from Sullom Voe to the USGC.
Mediterranean 80,000 tonners lost ground despite fresh chartering, descending to W95 from last done levels of W100.
In the inter-UKC sector rates on 80,000 tonners were steady around W100, with Lyondeall's chartering of the Nord Baltic at W100 seen as symptomatic for rates in the market.
The Caribbean saw rates settle around last done levels, North American brokers said
They said 70,000 tonners travelling up the U.S coast commanded rates of W130.

Bad weather in the region threatens shipping along the U.S. east coast and could hike rates, forecasters said on Friday. Hurricanes Edouard and Fran had caused several vessels to be delayed or to remain in port.
Brokers said that at least three ships had been affected, and that return journeys would be lengthened by about three days.
West African rates strengthened marginally amid slower chartering to the U.S and the East.
Suezmaxes to the U.S sustained their previous day's levels of W86.50 to W88.
